strings.name: Toyo Ito
strings.summary: Born in Japanese-ruled Seoul and raised in Japan, Ito graduated from the University of Tokyo and worked with Kiyonori Kikutake. From houses he moved toward experiments linking media, technology and nature. Tower of Winds, Sendai Mediatheque and Tama Art University Library explore lightness, flow and integrated structure. After the 2011 earthquake he joined Home-for-All reconstruction work, emphasizing community life. He won the 2013 Pritzker Prize.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Works including Sendai Mediatheque explore technology, nature and architectural structure, advancing formal innovation in public buildings and spatial design.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Keijo, Korea under Japanese rule; present-day Seoul, South Korea.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Graduated in architecture from the University of Tokyo in 1965.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Structure and flowing space
strings.highlights.h1.text: Sendai Mediatheque's tubular structures organize open floors and public activity.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Community and reconstruction
strings.highlights.h2.text: Collaborated with other architects on Home-for-All gathering places after the earthquake.
strings.timeline.t1.title: National Taichung Theater
strings.timeline.t1.text: The team's theater opened, extending experiments with continuous curved spaces.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Pritzker Architecture Prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: Recognized for architectural exploration of structure, space and public life.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Home-for-All
strings.timeline.t3.text: Joined community-space reconstruction after the Great East Japan Earthquake.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Tama Art University Library
strings.timeline.t4.text: Completed the Hachioji library, using arches to organize reading spaces.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Sendai Mediatheque opens
strings.timeline.t5.text: Open floors connect media, art and the public.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Tower of Winds
strings.timeline.t6.text: The Yokohama project used light and environmental responses to transform urban infrastructure.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Independent practice
strings.timeline.t7.text: Founded Urban Robot in Tokyo, later renamed Toyo Ito & Associates.
strings.timeline.t8.title: University of Tokyo graduation
strings.timeline.t8.text: Finished architecture studies and joined Kikutake's office.
